questions.stem: If a sorted array has 1024 elements, how many comparisons are needed in the worst case to find a target using binary search?
questions.explanation: Binary search reduces the search space by half each time. For 1024 elements, $\log_2(1024) = 10$ comparisons are needed in the worst case.

questions.stem: Explain why binary search is more efficient than linear search for large datasets.
markingGuide: Binary search has a time complexity of $O(\log n)$.
Linear search has a time complexity of $O(n)$.
Binary search reduces the search space by half each iteration.
For large datasets, the logarithmic growth of binary search is significantly faster than the linear growth of linear search.
questions.explanation: Binary search is more efficient because it reduces the search space exponentially, while linear search checks each element sequentially. This efficiency becomes more pronounced as the dataset size increases.

questions.stem: Discuss the impact of sorting on the efficiency of binary search when applied to an initially unsorted array.
markingGuide: Sorting an unsorted array takes $O(n \log n)$ time.
Binary search itself takes $O(\log n)$ time.
The overall time complexity becomes $O(n \log n)$ due to the sorting step.
Sorting is a one-time cost, but necessary for the efficiency of binary search.
questions.explanation: Sorting is a prerequisite for binary search. Although sorting adds an initial cost, it enables the efficient $O(\log n)$ search. The combined complexity is dominated by the sorting step.
